scope: Original practice for Hachiko, the SoFi skills article, and explanatory writing using the elephant reading.

pool.prompt: Which evidence best shows Kentaro’s feelings changed?
options: He goes from being nervous near Hachiko to bringing him food and water.
The train station stays in the same location.
The story mentions several adults.
Hachiko waits near a newspaper stand.
pool.rationale: Compare Kentaro’s early reaction with his later decision to care for Hachiko.

pool.prompt: What can Kentaro’s first-person narration tell a reader directly?
options: What Hachiko thinks when no one is there
What Kentaro observes and feels
What every person at the station believes
Exactly why Hachiko returns each day
pool.rationale: A first-person narrator reports personal thoughts and observations. The reader infers the thoughts of others from the text.

pool.prompt: What is the best way to support the idea that Hachiko’s waiting became important to the community?
options: Use a map of Tokyo to find the station.
List every adjective about Hachiko’s appearance.
Compare people helping him with the later effort to honor him.
Assume the dog understood each visitor’s thoughts.
pool.rationale: Actions taken by several people show that the story expands from one person’s care to a community response.

pool.prompt: Which statement gives an objective summary of the SoFi article?
options: SoFi is the most exciting robot ever invented.
The article is mainly about where ocean researchers live.
SoFi has solved every difficulty in underwater research.
A fish-shaped robot can observe marine life, and researchers identify limits that future designs could address.
pool.rationale: An objective summary includes the main development, evidence of usefulness, and limitations without adding opinion.

pool.prompt: Which detail best supports the idea that SoFi was built to observe ocean life?
options: It moves like a fish and records video underwater.
It has an easy-to-remember name.
One researcher worked at MIT.
Some parts were made with a 3-D printer.
pool.rationale: Its movement and camera explain directly how it can observe marine life.

pool.prompt: What is missing from the summary “Scientists made a robot called SoFi”?
options: A personal opinion about robots
What the robot helps researchers do and one important limitation
The name of every person in the article
A guess about a future version
pool.rationale: The main idea needs the robot’s purpose and a key qualification.

pool.prompt: Why does the SoFi article end with comments from other researchers?
options: To repeat the title in different words
To explain the exact steps for building the robot
To evaluate the robot’s promise and explain what still needs testing
To change the subject to a different invention
pool.rationale: The closing comments add outside evaluation and point out questions about longer and deeper trips.

pool.prompt: How does the design section develop the article’s main idea?
options: It tells readers which robot to buy.
It lists every fish species in the ocean.
It argues that future testing is unnecessary.
It explains features that help the robot swim and record video.
pool.rationale: The design details explain how SoFi could be used to observe marine life.

pool.prompt: Which description best captures the author’s purpose in the SoFi article?
options: Explain how the robot works and why it might help ocean research.
Persuade readers to buy an underwater camera.
Entertain with an invented adventure about a robot.
Prove that field scientists no longer need divers.
pool.rationale: The author presents a real design, its uses, and its limits to inform readers.

pool.prompt: Which thesis gives two clear points about how elephants respond to distress?
options: Elephants are animals that have been studied.
Observers sometimes reassure distressed elephants through physical contact and vocal behavior.
This essay will be about elephants.
Scientists looked at several interesting things.
pool.rationale: A thesis answers the prompt and provides two ideas the body paragraphs can explain.

pool.prompt: What should the bridge of an introduction do?
options: Introduce an unrelated example.
Repeat the last sentence of the conclusion.
Connect the hook to the topic and thesis.
Explain a new idea after the final paragraph.
pool.rationale: The bridge supplies the context readers need to get from the hook to the thesis.

pool.prompt: Which plan best follows a thesis about touch and sound as reassurance?
options: Both paragraphs list animal names.
The first paragraph changes the topic to ocean robots.
The two paragraphs repeat the thesis without evidence.
One body paragraph explains contact, and one explains vocal responses.
pool.rationale: Use each body paragraph to develop one point promised in the thesis.

pool.prompt: Which sentence is commentary about an elephant touching a distressed herd mate?
options: The contact supports the idea that an observer responded to the other animal’s distress.
The researchers watched a group of captive elephants.
The article describes elephants using their trunks.
This is the first paragraph of the essay.
pool.rationale: Commentary explains why a detail matters to the claim.

pool.prompt: Why should a summary of the elephant study say “the elephants observed” rather than “all elephants”?
options: The researchers never saw an elephant.
The evidence comes from a particular group under particular conditions.
An objective summary must avoid all nouns.
The article explains only how elephants eat.
pool.rationale: Limit a conclusion to the scope of the evidence.

pool.prompt: Which ending best fits an essay about touch and vocal behavior?
options: Add a new argument about how robots swim.
Copy the original thesis exactly and stop.
Restate both responses in new words and explain why researchers study them.
List the title and omit the two findings.
pool.rationale: The conclusion revisits both points and leaves readers with their significance.
